title: Anthropic Launches Enterprise-Managed Auth to Secure MCP Connectors
content_md: Anthropic has introduced enterprise-managed authorization for Model Context Protocol (MCP) connectors, allowing organizations to centrally provision, govern, and revoke Claude’s access to workplace applications through their identity provider. The capability removes a recurring obstacle in enterprise AI deployments: individual users previously had to approve each connector after an administrator enabled it. Under the new model, administrators authorize a connector once, map access to existing identity provider groups and roles, and users automatically receive the approved connections when they first sign in to Claude. Anthropic Launches Enterprise-Managed Auth Anthropic said the feature supports Datadog, Notion, and Slack, as well as Asana, Atlassian, Canva, Figma, Granola, Linear, and Supabase. Exa, Miro and Zoom support is expected next. MCP enables AI systems such as Claude to access external tools and enterprise context. However, every connection introduces an authorization boundary, potentially leading to unmanaged OAuth grants, long-lived credentials, inconsistent offboarding, and the risk of employees connecting personal accounts to corporate services. Anthropic’s implementation shifts connector authorization into the organization’s existing identity and access management workflow.
